captions.caption: Hubble's view of Proxima Centauri, a M-type dwarf and the nearest star to our Solar System. While this is the nearest star to the Sun, it was not discovered until 1915 due to its inherent faintness. Despite its proximity, it remains a point-like object in this image as even the closest stars to the Sun are very far away when compared to their physical size.
captions.alt_text: Proxima Centauri appears as a bright point with diffraction spikes. Several fainter stars are in the background.
